subject: Agriculture
title: Insect Farming
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Insect Farming.

hook.text: Black soldier fly larvae convert food waste into protein in 14 days. They eat garbage and become animal feed.

buildup.text: Insect farming requires 1,000 times less land and 500 times less water than beef production per kilogram of protein.

discovery.text: Insect protein is already used in fish feed and pet food. The EU approved mealworms for human consumption in 2021.

twist.text: Two billion people worldwide already eat insects regularly. The Western 'yuck factor' is cultural, not biological.

climax.text: Companies like Protix and InnovaFeed operate factory-scale insect farms producing thousands of tons of protein annually.

punchline.text: Feed waste to bugs, feed bugs to fish, feed fish to humans. Circular protein.

quiz.question: How does insect farming compare to beef in land use?
options: Requires 1,000 times less land per kilogram of protein
